summary: This diff (PROGRESS.md + ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml in compliance-tracker) is documentation-only and low blast radius, but it commits a verifiably false factual claim into the permanent governance ledger on a task whose entire mandate is confirming real status and zero duplication: it states 'this session's 4 new dispatch-gate files' were traced to 'currently-open PRs' #79, #80, #81, #82, and separately labels PR #81 as a 'still-open PR' whose HOLD_FOR_OWNER_SIGNOFF fix is 'not yet merged.' Live verification via `gh pr view 81` shows PR #81 is actually CLOSED (closedAt 2026-07-26T09:52:13Z, mergedAt null) -- rejected via an AUDIT: FAIL comment as 'fully duplicate, already-merged work' -- and it closed 9 minutes before this task's own closing commit (0b4c7d8c, 10:01:51Z), so the claim was already stale at the moment it was written. I also independently confirmed the underlying HOLD_FOR_OWNER_SIGNOFF field does not exist anywhere in the live-deployed /opt/veridian/scripts/veridian-task.py or supervisor-entrypoint.sh, so the practical conclusion ('not live yet') happens to still be directionally true, but the specific PR-state bookkeeping this task was dispatched to get right is wrong, and the same wrong 'open PR #81, not yet merged' framing was also carried into the actual work product, PR #83 on claude-control. Given the task's title is explicitly about re-verifying real status and confirming zero duplication, and PR #81 itself is a case of exactly the duplication this task was supposed to catch (it was closed for duplicating already-attempted work within its own redispatch history), this is a substantive correctness failure in the deliverable, not a cosmetic one. Recommend a quick follow-up: re-check current PR states for #79/#80/#81/#82 immediately before finalizing, correct the 'currently-open PRs' claim and the Engine 8 gap_description language in both this repo's PROGRESS.md/ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml and claude-control PR #83.
issues: PROGRESS.md claims this session traced 4 new files to 'currently-open PRs #79, #80, #81, #82' -- PR #81 is actually CLOSED (not merged, rejected as duplicate work), not open, as of gh pr view at review time.

ACTIVE-CLAIMS.yaml recently_completed entry repeats the same stale claim ('still-open PRs #81 ... and #82') into the permanent cross-session coordination registry, which other sessions rely on as ground truth per Rule 11 -- this risks a future session trusting a false 'pending merge' status for PR #81.

The same stale 'open PR #81, not yet merged' framing was carried into the actual engine-inventory work product (claude-control PR #83's gap_description for Engine 8), so the inaccuracy is not confined to this repo's tracking files.

PR #81 was itself closed for being duplicate/redundant work relative to an earlier commit in its own branch history -- this is exactly the class of duplication this task was dispatched to detect and confirm was absent, and it was missed.
